from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Coordinates are relative to an observer.",
            "A robot finds a box's location.",
            "Changing the grid alters the description.",
            "Physical location remains constant.",
            "Language changes, reality stays the same."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Intuitive Hook: The Observer's Perspective", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup visual elements
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-2, 5], y_range=[-2, 5], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        v = Vector([2, 3], color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(v, 'C3')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(Create(axes), GrowArrow(v))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        robot = Dot(color=RED).next_to(v.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)
        self.add(robot)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        rotated_axes = axes.copy().rotate(PI/6, about_point=axes.c2p(0, 0))
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(axes.copy(), rotated_axes))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(ORANGE))
        self.play(Indicate(v, color=WHITE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(PURPLE))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: Basis as Building Blocks", 
                          ["A basis is our building block.", 
                           "Vectors must be linearly independent.", 
                           "Standard basis uses cardinal directions."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display the standard basis vectors i, j (color #FFFFFF)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        origin = self.grid["D4"]
        i_vec = Arrow(origin, origin + RIGHT * 1.5, color=WHITE, buff=0)
        j_vec = Arrow(origin, origin + UP * 1.5, color=WHITE, buff=0)
        
        i_label = MathTex(r"\mathbf{i}", color=WHITE).next_to(i_vec.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        j_label = MathTex(r"\mathbf{j}", color=WHITE).next_to(j_vec.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(i_vec), Create(j_vec), Write(i_label), Write(j_label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Form a grid using i, j as the basis
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=(-2, 2, 1), y_range=(-2, 2, 1),
            x_length=3, y_length=3,
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": GREY, "stroke_width": 1}
        ).move_to(origin)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(grid), run_time=1.5)
        self.bring_to_front(i_vec, j_vec, i_label, j_label)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Introduce a new basis {b1, b2} (color #00FF00) as vectors
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        b1 = Arrow(origin, origin + (RIGHT + 0.5 * UP) * 1.5, color=GREEN, buff=0)
        b2 = Arrow(origin, origin + (-0.5 * RIGHT + UP) * 1.5, color=GREEN, buff=0)
        
        b1_label = MathTex(r"\mathbf{b}_1", color=GREEN).next_to(b1.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        b2_label = MathTex(r"\mathbf{b}_2", color=GREEN).next_to(b2.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(b1), Create(b2), Write(b1_label), Write(b2_label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Change of Basis Matrix (The 'Translator')", [
            "Need a translator between bases.",
            "Columns are the new basis vectors.",
            "Matrix P connects different grid overlays.",
            "Convert [v]_B to [v]_A.",
            "Compute [v]_A equals P times [v]_B."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Need a translator between bases.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Columns are the new basis vectors.
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        # Creating P matrix: [[1, 0], [1, 1]]
        p_matrix = Matrix([[1, 0], [1, 1]]).set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(p_matrix, 'B2', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(p_matrix))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Matrix P connects different grid overlays.
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        label = Text("P", font_size=24, color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(label, 'B1')
        self.play(Write(label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Convert [v]_B to [v]_A.
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00FFFF")
        v_b = MathTex(r"[v]_B").set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(v_b, 'D2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(v_b))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Compute [v]_A equals P times [v]_B.
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#00FFFF")
        equation = MathTex(r"[v]_A = P \cdot [v]_B").set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.place_in_area(equation, 'D3', 'F5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(equation))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["How do we reverse the translation?", "P-inverse takes us back to A.", "Grid stretches and shears together."]
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Inverse", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define base matrix visualization elements
        matrix_p = MathTex(r"P = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}", color="#00FFFF")
        matrix_inv = MathTex(r"P^{-1} = \begin{pmatrix} 0.5 & -0.5 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}", color="#FF00FF")
        
        # Grid representation (using lines)
        grid_lines = VGroup()
        for i in range(-2, 3):
            line_h = Line(start=np.array([-1, 0, 0]), end=np.array([1, 0, 0]), color=GRAY)
            line_v = Line(start=np.array([0, -1, 0]), end=np.array([0, 1, 0]), color=GRAY)
            grid_lines.add(line_h.shift(i * 0.4 * UP), line_v.shift(i * 0.4 * RIGHT))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_p, "B4")
        self.play(Write(matrix_p))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_inv, "D4")
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix_inv))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_in_area(grid_lines, "B5", "E6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(grid_lines))
        
        # Animate "stretch and shear"
        self.play(
            grid_lines.animate.apply_matrix([[0.5, -0.5], [0, 1]]),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Mastering the Change of Basis in Linear Algebra

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The Observer's Perspective
sections.content: Introduce the concept that coordinates are relative to an observer (the basis). Use a 'Robot Delivery' analogy: The robot needs to find a box. If we change the 'grid' the robot uses to see the world, the coordinate numbers change, but the physical location remains identical.
sections.example: A robot at coordinate (2, 3) in Basis A. If we rotate the grid to Basis B, the robot is still at the same spot, but now reads as (1, 4). The 'where' is constant; the 'description' changes.

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Basis as Building Blocks
sections.content: Briefly define a basis as a set of linearly independent vectors that span the space. Use a visual representation of the Standard Basis (i, j) vs. a Non-Standard Basis (u, v) represented by vectors pointing in different directions.
sections.example: Standard Basis vectors are like the cardinal directions (North, East). A new basis is like using (Northeast, Northwest) to describe the same field.

sections.title: The Change of Basis Matrix (The 'Translator')
sections.content: Explain that moving from Basis B to Basis A requires a matrix P, where the columns are the Basis B vectors expressed in terms of Basis A coordinates. Visualize this as a 'transformation bridge' connecting two different grid overlays on the same 2D plane.
sections.example: To convert coordinates [v]_B to [v]_A, compute [v]_A = P * [v]_B. If Basis B is { (1,1), (0,1) }, the matrix P = [[1, 0], [1, 1]].

sections.title: Visualizing the Inverse
sections.content: Discuss how to go back. If P takes us from B to A, P-inverse takes us from A to B. Show an animation where the coordinate grid 'stretches' and 'shears' to match the new basis.
sections.example: If the robot reports its position in local grid coordinates (Basis B), we multiply by P-inverse to get its position on our global map (Standard Basis A).

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
sections.content: Recap: Change of basis is a change of language, not a change of reality. Emphasize that finding the 'right' basis can simplify complex physics/engineering problems (e.g., diagonalizing matrices).
sections.example: Final shot: A complex vector spinning in space; changing the basis allows us to view the rotation as a simple projection on one axis—making the math 10x easier.
